note: Verifies the cancellation / cleanup / observability CONTRACTS of GraphQL.js v17 against the v16 baseline. Each row is a deterministic behavior observation (throw vs resolve, event ordering, channel payload shape), not a timing sample — so no statistical distribution applies. Millisecond figures are machine-dependent context, never an evidence claim.
subject: graphql 17.0.1

behaviors_verified.claim: In v16, passing an abortSignal to execute() is silently ignored: both fields resolve to full data and info.getAbortSignal does not exist.
behaviors_verified.baseline_v16: resolved (slow=slow-result, slowCooperative=coop-result); getAbortSignal:undefined; ran to the ~300ms timers

behaviors_verified.claim: In v17, execute({abortSignal}) rejects with AbortedGraphQLExecutionError the moment abort() fires (~80ms), before the ~300ms resolvers finish.

v17 cancellation is COOPERATIVE. The executor stops waiting and throws, but child work only stops if the resolver forwards info.getAbortSignal(). A non-propagating resolver's work continues as an orphan.
behaviors_verified.observed: event log shows db:abort:coop (cooperative child actually cancelled, no db:done:coop) while db:done:slow still fires AFTER abort (non-propagating child runs to completion)

behaviors_verified.claim: Cancelling a mutation is not a transaction rollback. With sequential top-level mutation fields, an abort mid-flight still lets already-started side effects commit; the caller receives only the AbortedGraphQLExecutionError and cannot tell which writes landed.
behaviors_verified.observed: events A:enter -> A:wrote -> B:enter -> B:wrote despite abort at 90ms; execute threw AbortedGraphQLExecutionError (isAborted=true) with no partial data telling the caller both wrote

behaviors_verified.claim: v17 publishes a node:diagnostics_channel TracingChannel surface: named channels for parse / validate / execute / execute:variableCoercion / execute:rootSelectionSet / resolve / subscribe, each with start/end/asyncStart/asyncEnd/error, and graphql:resolve carries a rich per-field payload.
behaviors_verified.observed: channels fired in order execute -> variableCoercion -> rootSelectionSet -> resolve (per field) -> rootSelectionSet:end -> execute:end, then async fields as asyncStart/asyncEnd; graphql:resolve start payload keys = [alias, args, fieldName, fieldPath, fieldType, isDefaultResolver, parentType]
behaviors_verified.caveat: This run called execute() on a pre-parsed document, so the parse pair observed comes from setup and graphql:validate did NOT fire (validation is a separate stage from execution). The full parse->validate->execute chain appears only when using graphql()/the whole pipeline.

behaviors_verified.claim: On abort, v17 preserves the partial result out-of-band: error.cause carries the abort reason and error.abortedResult resolves to an ExecutionResult where completed fields keep their value and cut-off fields are null with a path error.
behaviors_verified.observed: caught AbortedGraphQLExecutionError; cause.message='client gone'; abortedResult = { data:{fast:'FAST', slow:null}, errors:[{path:['slow']}] }

timings_context_only.note: Not evidence. Recorded only to show the fast-fail gap. Drifts per machine.

cited_not_measured.claim: The diagnostics tracing is zero-overhead when nobody subscribes (shouldTrace gates on channel.hasSubscribers).
cited_not_measured.source: graphql 17 diagnostics.mjs source; this run always had subscribers, so the no-subscriber cost was read from source, not measured.

cited_not_measured.claim: Whether a real database driver honors an AbortSignal depends on the driver.
cited_not_measured.source: The probe uses a setTimeout fake DB to prove the propagation MECHANISM; real-driver cooperation is stated as a caveat in the post, not measured here.

cited_not_measured.claim: @defer / @stream incremental delivery remains an experimental, separate surface in v17.
cited_not_measured.source: GraphQL.js v17 release notes; out of scope for this run.
